written: 2026-11-25, before rerun.py existed; see the commit that adds this file
rule: A case passes when status, every command outcome, every output class, every listed flag and the reproduced list all match exactly. 'reproduced' is the set of declared outputs a receipt may call reproduced: rewritten during this run by a command that exited 0, and equal to the committed file (identical) or equal in every number within rel_tol with the same text (numbers-match). The naive baseline calls every declared output of an exit-0 command reproduced.

classes.identical: rewritten in this run, bytes equal to the committed file
classes.numbers-match: rewritten, same text, every number within rel_tol of the committed one, bytes differ
classes.numbers-differ: rewritten, same text skeleton, at least one number outside rel_tol
classes.text-differs: rewritten, non-numeric text differs from the committed file
classes.not-rewritten: committed file present and not written by this run (possible replay of a committed result)
classes.no-reference: produced, but nothing committed to compare with

cases.note: added 2026-11-25 before converters existed: a binary file whose header names the writer's version differs in bytes; after the spec's converter, content is equal, so numbers-match, not identical

receipt_text_rules: The rendered RECEIPT.md never contains the words wrong, incorrect, error in the paper, or fails to replicate.
Every output in 'reproduced' and no other is described as reproduced.
Every command that did not exit 0 appears under 'Failed, stopped or killed runs' with its log path.
The receipt names the commit, each command exactly as run, the OS, CPU, cores, RAM, tool versions, wall clock and run cost.
An aborted run says no package code ran.
